Scope: roads and paving, potable water, TSE, sewer, storm water, irrigation and landscaping, electrical (medium voltage, telecom, street lighting) and CCTV networks in Zones A and G, over 18 months.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. On 02-Nov-2026 the project is 46.7% complete against 43.6% planned, 3.1% ahead (SPI 1.07). This week it gained only 0.32% against 1.48% planned, all of it in road works, so the lead narrowed from 4.3% to 3.1%, the third weekly drop in a row. Road works and the storm and sewer networks are still ahead; procurement, engineering, electrical works and CCTV are behind.

Ahead overall, but progress almost stalled this week and procurement is still behind. This week's progress (0.32%) was less than a quarter of the weekly plan (1.48%): storm water, sewer, electrical and CCTV works earned no man-hours, and no quantity was added in the Major Quantities sheet. Procurement is at 60.4% against 99.6% planned (SPI 0.61): MV cables (0 of 51,500 m), unit substations, street lighting poles and lighting panels are still not delivered, and the final substation location is still pending between the Client and SEC. The P6 update still finishes the project on 05-Jul-2027 with zero float, and finishing works now have only 2.7 days of float.

The weekly report and the P6 update disagree on four milestone dates, and the finishing works are now close to the contract date. Mobilisation finished on 05-Feb-2026 in the weekly report but on 06-Apr-2026 in P6. Technical submittals finished on 16-Aug-2026 in the weekly report but on 25-Jul-2026 in P6. The weekly report forecasts the engineering phase to finish on 28-Sep-2026, while P6 still has it open on 01-Nov-2026. Procurement finishes on 17-Jan-2027 in the weekly report and 04-Jan-2027 in P6. In this week's P6 update road works moved 3 days later, to 13 days after their baseline (float 12 days), finishing works moved 4 days later (float 2.7 days, from 5.7), and MV works moved 2 days earlier (25-Feb-2027, float 25 days). Project finish has no float left.

Data notes

  • The uploaded files name the project "Phase Two – Part Two" (SUD1-02-011), while the repository folder and the project tracker call it Phase 3 (المرحلة الثالثة).
  • The summary sheet labels cost-based progress as "Plan" and "Actual". This report uses physical progress (man-hour weighted) only: 43.63% planned and 46.74% actual.
  • The Physical-Chart Data sheet's baseline plans 44.2% at 06-Oct and 52.5% at 06-Nov, well above the 43.63% planned to 02-Nov on the front sheet, and it shows the 02-Nov actual (46.74%) on the 06-Nov point. Measured against that chart baseline the project would be behind plan.
  • The front sheet leaves physical progress for electrical, landscape and CCTV works blank; the man-hours in the Progress sheet were used. Its BOQ values for CCTV Zone A and Zone G read 46,056 and 2 SAR instead of 6,513,996 and 2,791,854.
  • The P6 update has a data date of 01-Nov-2026, one day before the weekly report (02-Nov-2026). Its activity counts match the schedule panel (800 completed, 354 in progress, 961 not started), but the front sheet still shows 144 in progress.
  • The weekly report puts the procurement phase baseline at 23-Jan-2027; the approved baseline schedule (uploaded with the 19-Oct report) has 21-Nov-2026.
  • The summary page's scope table shows 0 executed for every network, and its totals differ from the hidden Conclusion sheet (for example roads 15,234 m vs 18,252 m). Manholes are labelled "m" in the Major Quantities sheet but are counted in units.
  • Procurement figures disagree: street lighting poles are 590 units and 10% complete in the Procurement sheet but 592 units with 1 delivered in Major Quantities; LV cables are 29,700 m vs 68,400 m. MV cables are "not submitted" in procurement, while the risk register says they have been procured.
  • The manpower sheet reports the same actual head count for November as for October (607). November planned head count is 391 in the monthly table (365 manual, 26 non-manual) but 390 in the head-count panel (350 manual, 40 non-manual).
  • Several cells show #REF! errors (EAC, risk scores, safety score in the status score). The substation risk carries a value of 6,835,460.61 SAR, which is the landscape BOQ value.
  • Several sheets (front sheet header, Major Quantities, Milestones, Physical-Chart Data) still carry 19-Oct-2026 as their date, although the report's data date is 02-Nov-2026. The Major Quantities and Procurement sheets are unchanged from 26-Oct. Two of the six photos in the photo sheet are under 600 px wide and were left out. The report week is the contract week the report states (43 of 78); whole weeks since handover give 42.
